column3: NASB renders the imperfect as “had been saying.”
NASB supplies “Herod” and “John”; “were holding him as a prophet” is “regarded John as a prophet.”
NASB renders “in the midst” as “before them.”
NASB follows the critical text (“although he was grieved”); “those reclining with him” is rendered “his dinner guests.”
NASB follows the critical text with “the body” and “it.”
NASB adds “about John” and renders “the crowds” as “the people” and “towns” as “cities.”
NASB has “He,” not “Jesus,” like the critical text, and renders “gone out” as “went ashore.”
NASB has “the disciples” without “His,” like the critical text; “the time is gone by” is rendered “the hour is already late.”
NASB renders “the crowds” as “the people,” adds “the food” to “blessed,” and repeats “gave them.”
NASB has “He” and “the disciples” without “Jesus” and “His,” like the critical text; “compelled” is rendered “made.”
NASB follows the critical text: “a long distance from the land” (literally “many stadia”); the Textus Receptus has “in the midst of the sea.” “Tormented” is rendered “battered.”
NASB follows the critical text with “He” (not “Jesus”).
NASB follows the critical text (“came toward Jesus”).
NASB follows the reading without “strong” (“the wind”), which the critical text includes in brackets.
